title: Model ingestion runtime-hints and deployment acceptance criteria
creator: Olivia Chen
description: Clarify required metadata, runtime hints, and acceptance tests for new open-model ingestion into the Redwood model catalog. This ticket narrows scope to the onboarding contract (what we require from model submitters and what the runtime needs to determine compatibility automatically). Goal: reduce back-and-forth during intake, enable safe unpinned deployments with deterministic fallback behavior, and provide minimal telemetry consent patterns for community weights.
acceptance_criteria: A clear required metadata schema is documented and validated by the intake service: architecture (decoder/encoder/mix), expected max_sequence, autorollback_safe flag, quantization_compat hints (int8/4bit), and preferred_kernel_tags.
Define and publish a Runtime Hint Taxonomy (three-tier): REQUIRED, RECOMMENDED, ADVISORY. Intake validates REQUIRED fields and surfaces RECOMMENDED warnings.

Unpinned model policy: if 'autorollback_safe' is true and runtime_compat_score >= 0.85, model may be offered unpinned in canary mode; otherwise onboarding must include a pinned fallback variant. The policy is codified and testable in the intake contract.

Fallback rules: Runtime will attempt up to 2 variant fallbacks (quantized -> non-quantized -> smaller-seq) before rejecting a request; behavior visible in the catalog entry and traceable in Console traces.

Acceptance tests: automated intake CI that runs a lightweight sanity generation (3 prompts) and a KV-cache warmup trace; results stored on the intake PR and must pass stability thresholds (no OOM, tokens generated within latency budget for a 512 token request on target instance class).

Telemetry opt-in: community-weight submitters must provide a consent string and a minimal telemetry URL; intake must record consent and surface it on the model page. Consent implementation must be documented for legal and privacy review.
Docs: PRD and intake checklist links are present in the intake UI and the onboarding PR. UX copy for 'unproofed' vs 'pinned' variants is approved by developer experience team.
Security: any model marked 'sensitive-data' requires KMS integration verification and manual security sign-off; the intake system blocks submission without required artifacts.
Rollout plan: configuration to enable new taxonomy and policy behind a feature flag; a rollout checklist exists for private and dedicated customers to opt-out during initial 3-week canary window.
Sign-offs: PM, Eng runtime lead, Security, and Developer Experience must approve the intake contract before merging.
Updated intake API spec (openapi link) published and added to the model ingestion SDK with examples for community submitters.
out_of_scope: Full model performance benchmarking (this remains under runtime E2E perf initiative).
Automatic retraining or weight transformation pipelines for incompatible community variants.
UI rework of the full model catalog browse experience (only intake flow copy and the single model page will be updated).
risks: Over-constraining metadata could discourage community submissions — mitigate with clear fallback paths and a lightweight 'experimental' intake path.
False positives in runtime_compat_score could allow unstable variants into unpinned canaries — mitigate with conservative thresholds and canary autoscaling caps.
Telemetry opt-in complexity may delay legal approval — engage Legal early and provide minimal default telemetry schema.
Runtime behavior differences across Dedicated/Private deployments may cause mismatches in on-paper compatibility — provide explicit per-deployment notes and a runtime-agnostic compatibility label.
decisions: Adopt three-tier Runtime Hint Taxonomy (REQUIRED/RECOMMENDED/ADVISORY) to balance strictness and flexibility.
Require at least one pinned fallback variant for any model that opts out of 'autorollback_safe'.
Feature-flag rollout for the policy to allow fast rollback if we observe catalog-level regressions.
